The search turned up release notes for the `agents` package (v0.22.0) that cover this option. I didn't find the official API reference for it, so the details below come from the changelog.

**Default throttling:** Streaming writes chat state once per chunk, and each write re-renders. When chunks arrive in a burst, React can hit its render limit. The changelog says this happens when chunks arrive in a burst — a resumed stream replaying a long turn, for example, and the AI SDK then reports a completed turn as failed.

**What changed:** useAgentChat now coalesces those updates every 50ms, which removes about 78% of renders on a fast stream and matches the value the AI SDK documents. The first chunk of a stream is never delayed.

**Configuration:** To change this, you pass a `throttle` option. Pass throttle: false to render every chunk as it arrives, or a number to change the interval.

**Deprecated option:** The deprecated experimental_throttle is still honoured. If your code uses it, it should keep working, but you should move to `throttle`.

**Stale content:** Message snapshots, functional updates, and streamed continuations resolve against the current chat store, so coalescing renders cannot roll assistant content back to an older snapshot.

If you need the exact type signature or the default behavior in your version, check the `@cloudflare/ai-chat` package docs or its changelog for your installed release.

content.text:
It depends on your version. Starting with the `agents@0.22.0` release, `useAgentChat` throttles by default. It batches streamed updates into one render every 50ms, which is the same interval the AI SDK documents. The first chunk of a stream still renders right away. Before that release, it updated chat state on every chunk. That could set off a burst of re-renders, for example when a resumed stream replayed a long turn, and React could hit its render limit. To change the behavior, pass `throttle: false` to render every chunk, or a number to set a different interval in milliseconds. The older `experimental_throttle` option is deprecated but still works.

I got this from the release notes, not the API reference. If you're on the newer `@cloudflare/ai-chat` package, check its changelog for your installed version.

Sources:
- [cloudflare/agents agents@0.22.0 release notes](https://newreleases.io/project/github/cloudflare/agents/release/agents@0.22.0)
- [@cloudflare/ai-chat@0.9.4 release](https://newreleases.io/project/github/cloudflare/agents/release/@cloudflare%2Fai-chat@0.9.4)
